item.description: India's healthcare market could approach ₹12 lakh crore by 2030, but new drugs, AI, outpatient care and prevention could change where patients are treated — and where the industry makes money.

item.description: The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which has been passed by the Parliament this month, provides for a time-bound resolution of payment disputes and stronger enforcement of awards.

item.title: Opening a cinema hall in Delhi just got easier as govt scraps maze of multiple NOCs
item.description: Delhi's new online system replaces multiple departmental approvals with coordinated inspections and fixed timelines, potentially making it faster for multiplex operators to open new screens.
item.dc:creator: Megha Rani

item.title: Why private equity is pouring billions into Indian hospitals — and what policymakers are worried about
item.description: India’s hospital sector is attracting billions in private equity as demand for beds, specialised care and advanced medical technology rises. While investors argue that PE capital is helping hospitals expand and modernise, policymakers are examining whether financial incentives could affect affordability, pricing and patient care. The challenge is to ensure private capital expands healthcare capacity without compromising access or transparency.
item.dc:creator: Swapnil Deshpande

item.title: India set for record soyoil imports as Russia-Ukraine war disrupts sunflower shipments
item.description: Soyoil imports in August are likely to rise to 620,000 metric tons, nearly 46% above the average monthly imports of 424,549 tons so far in the current marketing year, which began in November, according to four traders directly involved in trade deals. The traders did not wish to be named in line with their companies' policies.
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jha
